Aharon-Benyamin Mazuz, son of Sara and Nisim, was born on 1 Iyar 5716 (12 April 1956) in Rehovot. He attended the Netiv Eliyahu elementary school in Netivot and then spent one year in the metalwork track at the Torah VeMelacha vocational school in Netivot. After completing his studies, Aharon-Benyamin worked at a variety of jobs: briefly polishing diamonds, and for most of the time in construction work, as a formworker and plasterer.

Aharon-Benyamin was a friendly and cheerful young man, content with his lot. He loved practical jokes and was known for a well-developed sense of humor; at the same time, he acted with integrity and conscience in serious matters of importance. He was a devoted and loyal son to his parents, looked after his family, and helped support the household.

Aharon-Benyamin was drafted into the IDF on 8 April 1974 into the Maintenance Corps. After basic training, and after completing various professional courses, including a course in driving a tracked vehicle and a course in driving heavy vehicles, he was posted to the Sinai region as a transport driver. He was a dedicated and loyal soldier in his role. Aharon-Benyamin was known among his commanders and comrades as an excellent driver, devoted to his duties and responsible. He mastered the heavy vehicle assigned to him with ease, looked after it properly, and carried out his tasks in all weather conditions. He was a careful driver.

On 6 Av 5736 (2 August 1976), he fell while carrying out his duties. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Netivot. He is survived by his parents, three brothers and two sisters. In a letter of condolence to the family, his commander wrote: "Aharon-Benyamin was one of the best soldiers in the unit. He influenced and led his comrades in arms on difficult roads, displaying leadership, initiative and responsibility worthy of praise."
